note: A verdict and a reason for every ambiguous-ownership domain in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json's bothDivergent list: Express registers handlers for it, an edge function serves it, and nothing proxies between them, so dev and production run different code for the same path. 'unexamined' is a permitted verdict and is the point - it is what stops a guess from being written down as a finding, and this file exists because two priority-1 stories (LAUNCH-013, LEGAL-004) sat inside the flat list indistinguishable from the entries where the divergence is harmless. VERDICTS: parity (both hosts checked, same behaviour); divergent (a named behavioural difference that matters in production); resolved (was divergent, ported, with the round named); express-only-capability (Express does something the edge does not and that is a recorded gap); unexamined (nobody has compared them). Added round 124. A domain that stops being ambiguous - usually because the prefix was proxied - LEAVES this file, so the 'resolved' count is not a history of everything ever fixed; it is the domains that were ported while the divergence itself remains. Round 134 dropped catalog and enabled-products on porting them, and dropped mobile (round 113) and onboarding (round 133), whose scoped proxy entries had made them unambiguous without anyone tightening docs/route-ownership-baseline.json - a stale entry here is pre-forgiveness for whatever lands under that name next.

chatbot.reason: Round 153 read both. The six console paths (connections, connect, links, query-log) ran on an Express copy with no role check while the edge function needs a MANAGER to change an install or a mapping; they are proxied with scoped entries and the Express handlers deleted. POST /query stays Express-only on purpose - the edge function answers 501 CHATBOT_QUERY_NOT_PORTED because the tool registry needs CLAUDE_API_KEY at the edge - and its caller-supplied platformUserId could resolve to another user's scope, now refused unless the link is the caller's own.

database-updater.reason: Round 166 read both. Express mounts server/database-updater/api/updater-routes.ts behind platformAdminRoute and drives DatabaseUpdaterManager, an in-process Node scheduler whose registry, cron timers and config live in memory - real on a developer machine. The edge function could not run it and answered 200 success:true to all seven controls the two admin pages call (start, stop, execute, enable, disable, dry-run, plus config) while doing nothing, and status said isRunning:false, which both pages render as a STOPPED system with a working Start button. Now status answers available:false with code UPDATER_NOT_ON_EDGE and every control answers 501 with that code; DatabaseManagement and DatabaseUpdaterPage show the reason and disable Start. NOT proxied on purpose: proxying would take the only working host away from dev. Two things left open: DatabaseUpdaterPage reads totalJobs/runningJobs/jobs/systemHealth, which getStatus() has never returned on either host (it answers isRunning/updaters/nextExecutions/config inside a {success,data} envelope), so that page renders zeroes even in dev; and the edge gate admits level 7 or can_access_all_tenants while Express requires platform admin.

deal-stages.reason: Round 138. One client path: LeadDeals.tsx GETs /api/deal-stages for the stage dropdown. Both hosts read deal_stages scoped to tenant_id ordered by sort_order and answer a bare array; the edge function layers sortOrder/isActive camel aliases over the snake row and Express returns the Drizzle row, and the page reads through extractRecords, so the live path is at parity. Express additionally has POST /api/deal-stages and POST /api/deal-stages/initialize (routes-workflow-mobile.ts:552, :571) with NO caller in any of the seven client trees - the edge function is GET-only. Note deal_stages is the LEGACY stage model (deals.stage_id holds a deal_stages.id; pipeline_stages.legacy_stage_id is CRMX-005's bridge), so a second write path into it is not work worth porting, and server/lib/pipeline-stage-mirror.ts already records those two endpoints as legacy creators. Nothing is broken on either host.

equipment.reason: Round 131. Every path a client tree calls - GET /api/equipment, /:id, /:id/meter-readings, /:id/service-history - has a branch in supabase/functions/equipment/. The Express extras have NO caller anywhere: routes-equipment-qr.ts (/:id/qr-code, /:id/asset-label, POST /bulk-qr-codes) mounted at routes-registry:820, routes-bulk-operations.ts (/bulk-update, /bulk-delete), routes-warehouse.ts (/:id/lifecycle) and routes-workflow-mobile.ts (/:id/trigger-service) - grepped across all seven client trees plus ios. The edge function already refuses an unknown sub-resource with a 404 above its /:id branch (round 115), so a POST to any of those Express-only paths cannot fall into the CREATE branch and write a junk equipment row, which was the first thing checked.

gdpr.reason: Round 123. The Express service erased a data subject's uploaded objects across six buckets with Art. 17(3) exemptions named per bucket; the edge function anonymised two tables of rows, touched no storage, and answered 'User data has been anonymized'. import.reason: CORRECTED round 170. This entry used to say requireFeature('ai_csv_import') gated the AI import paths on Express only, leaving them open to any tenant regardless of plan in production. Reading supabase/functions/import/ says otherwise: it has no AI client at all. GET /ai/status answers available:false, POST /ai/map-columns answers 503 'AI refinement is not available on this deployment', and /jobs/:id/ai-process has no branch, so there is nothing a plan flag would gate. The real difference is capability, not policy: Express can run AI column mapping for a plan that has ai_csv_import, and production cannot run it for anyone. import-ai-plan-gate.test.ts fails the day the edge function gains an AI branch without a feature or plan check, which is when this becomes a policy gap.

integrations.reason: Round 176 CORRECTED this entry and closed its dev half. The note said routes-integrations.ts registers GET /api/integrations/:id and so shadows /marketplace; it has no such handler (stale). What it DID register, mounted ahead of integrations/routes.ts, was GET /api/integrations, PUT /:id and POST /:id/test, and it won all three - so PA-053's honest handlers over platform_integrations never ran in dev. Dev listed system_integrations instead (a different table from the one production reads), and the test route wrote status 'connected' - not in that column's active|inactive|error|pending vocabulary - and answered 'Connection test successful' without testing anything. routes-integrations.ts is deleted, as is the importer-less routes-integrations-real.ts, and integrations-one-express-router.test.ts asserts one Express registrant per path. WHAT REMAINS is the capability gap round 129 recorded: the OAuth connect flow completes on Express (session-bound state and tokens) and the edge function answers 501 OAUTH_STATE_IS_SESSION_BOUND. useExternalIntegrations' paths are still unserved on the edge, but its only consumer is an orphan page.

quickbooks.reason: Round 126 read both. Express runs the real Intuit OAuth flow and holds the access token, refresh token and company id in req.session, under its own comment 'in a real app, save to database' - so it works on a developer machine and writes no row. The edge function read `integrations` and `quickbooks_mappings`, both phantom, DISCARDED the error on GET /status and answered connected:false at 200, so every dealer in production was told they had not connected QuickBooks whether or not they had. Both hosts also reported a sync that persists nothing: the edge branches never called Intuit ('in production, this would call the QuickBooks API') and Express called it, transformed the result and dropped it ('in a real implementation, save to database here') while answering 'Successfully synced N customers'. All sync paths on BOTH hosts now answer 501 SYNC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED from shared/quickbooks-availability.ts, and the edge status answers connected:null with CONNECTION_NOT_STORED. WHAT REMAINS IS THE CAPABILITY GAP: Express can start and complete the OAuth flow and production cannot, because the state and the tokens are session-bound - GET /quickbooks/connect has 501'd with OAUTH_STATE_IS_SESSION_BOUND since EDGE-002h for that reason. Closing it means a credential store plus moving OAuth state into a table, which is a redesign rather than a port.

rbac.reason: Round 127 read both. PROD-013's two recorded defects were already fixed - the roles branch answers {roles, pagination} off tenant-scoped enhanced_roles and permissions answers {permissions, groupedPermissions, totalCount} - so that half of this entry was stale. The live finding was larger: ROLE MANAGEMENT HAS NEVER BEEN INITIALIZABLE ON ANY HOST. GET /rbac/status gates the page on enhanced_roles holding a row, the only writer is POST /rbac/seed, and that 501'd on the edge function while dying on its first INSERT on Express - it omitted lft/rght/depth, organizational_tier and created_by (all NOT NULL, no default), wrote 'COMPANY'/'INDIVIDUAL' into role_hierarchy_level (level_1..level_8) and 'COMPANY' into organizational_tier (lowercase), and named four role codes migration 0072's catalogue does not carry. shared/rbac-seed.ts now builds the rows for both hosts, deriving every level from the catalogue and computing the nested set, and the edge seed is gated on the global roles level (gating on enhanced_roles would be circular on a tenant that has none). Also rebound: rbac_audit_log was phantom on BOTH the assign-role write (whose result was never destructured) and the audit-logs read (which discarded its error and answered [] - 'nobody has changed anyone's access' on a security screen); both use audit_logs through _shared/audit-log.ts now, ordered by `timestamp` rather than created_at. The phantom-tables baseline is one entry shorter.

root-admin.reason: Round 167 read both for the twelve paths client/src calls. Five - signups, signups-analytics, trial-funnel, high-value-signups, pending-tasks - were served ONLY by the edge function: routes-signup-crm.ts is mounted at /api/root-admin/crm, which nothing calls, and routes-root-admin.ts registers none of them, so the signups CRM and the command centre's pending-task list 404'd in dev while working in production. They are scoped crmProxies entries now. system-resources, database-tables and execute-query stay Express-only on purpose: the edge function refuses them with REQUIRES_DIRECT_SQL because they introspect Postgres and execute-query depends on SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY. Separately, Express GET /security/locked-accounts and POST /security/unlock-account had no requireRootAdmin, so any authenticated member of any tenant could list every locked account and clear any brute-force lockout (login_attempts has no tenant_id); both are gated and a test asserts every handler in that file is. NOT YET COMPARED: overview, tenants, security-alerts and audit-logs are served by both hosts and their response shapes have not been checked against each other. The /crm router's signups/:id, PATCH, log-activity and send-email have no caller in any client tree.

seo.reason: Round 169 read the routing. Every /api/seo segment client/src calls (settings, pages, page-scores, keywords, alerts, competitors, crawl and crawl/results, audit and audit/history, core-web-vitals, sitemap/generate, analyze/images, check/broken-links|mobile|security, validate/structured-data, detect/redirect-chains) has a branch in supabase/functions/seo/. routes-seo.ts carried three shadowed or wrong-domain duplicates, all deleted: GET/POST /api/seo/settings (routes-seo-core.ts registers both first, at routes-registry:320 against :774), per-request /sitemap.xml and /robots.txt on https://printyx.com (shadowed by the committed files SEO-006 made canonical), and a LIVE /image-sitemap.xml on that same wrong domain that nothing links to. seo-artifact-single-writer.test.ts asserts one Express writer per path. STILL NOT COMPARED: the response shapes of the remaining list and action endpoints on the two hosts. The edge side projects every list row through _shared/seo-projection.ts to camelCase (PROD-014) and Express returns Drizzle rows, so they are likely at parity, but nobody has checked field by field.

subscriptions.reason: Round 168 compared the sixteen paths client/src calls; all live in one hook, useSubscription.ts, and both hosts serve all sixteen. Status, create, upgrade, cancel, convert-trial and notifications were already locked by the subscription-*-shape and subscription-status-parity tests. GET /plans was not and was divergent: the edge function answered raw snake_case rows while Pricing.tsx, the one consumer, reads the camelCase keys Drizzle gives Express, so production priced every plan at $NaN, never showed Most Popular, left every limit blank and offered no trial. Both lists are camelised now and subscription-plans-shape.test.ts derives the expected keys from the table declaration. /usage (useUsageStats) has no consumer, so its shape was not compared. The Stripe paths (checkout, addon, session, portal, setup-intent, preview-upgrade, stripe/config) were matched key for key in PROD-STRIPE-001 and not re-read. The twelve Express gates LAUNCH-013 recorded remain dead in production and are tracked in docs/dead-policy-gates-baseline.json; the Stripe webhook at /subscriptions/webhooks/stripe is why the prefix cannot simply be proxied.

task-workflows.reason: Round 138. Four routed pages (WorkflowsListPage, WorkflowBuilderPage, WorkflowDetailPage, WorkflowStepPage) drive 11 paths; supabase/functions/task-workflows/ serves ten of them and server/routes-task-workflows.ts serves all eleven. THE NAMED DIFFERENCE IS POST /parse: uploading an image/CSV/XLSX and having it parsed into a draft needs multipart plus exceljs and the Anthropic SDK, so it is deliberately Express-only and the edge function answers 501 - which is why the prefix is not proxied (an entry would take /parse from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev). Round 138 made that refusal readable: the page toasted the server's sentence wrapped in the JSON it arrived in, titled 'Parse failed' in red, so a backend that does not do this read as a broken feature; it now says 'Upload not available here' with the reason, via client/src/lib/api-error.ts. THE STATE MACHINE WAS THE REAL RISK AND IS CLOSED: the edge function carried a 40-line replica of shared/task-workflow-state.ts under a note claiming Deno could not import from shared/ (it can), while the engine imported three of ten exports and hand-inlined the rest - so three implementations of the advance/regress/completion math existed and server/tests/unit/task-workflow-state.test.ts pinned the one neither host ran. Both hosts now import and call the one module, and server/tests/unit/task-workflow-shared-state.test.ts fails if either grows its own copy. Everything else was compared and agrees: routing, the notification pair (email + user_notifications; the Node WebSocket broadcast has no prod consumer per PA-030), and the task_workflow_event_type vocabulary, whose 12 values are all in migration 0009's CREATE TYPE.

technician-management.reason: Round 92. All five edge writes were ungated while the Express twin checked SERVICE.TECHNICIAN.MANAGE - dev was the safe host and production the open one. The edge function carries eight gate calls now.
